name: Ms. Dustdevil
role: Clears away what nobody uses any more — and straightens what hangs crooked
greet.2: Tsk — who left all this lying around?
greet.4: Don't worry, I never throw anything out — it all goes into my storeroom first. You never know.
greet.5: A place for everything, and everything in its place!
greet.6: A container without a picture? That simply won't do!
fit.yes: Ms. Dustdevil is already rolling up her sleeves: "Docker? Then there's dust somewhere — I'll find it!"
fire_note: Whatever is in her storeroom stays there until you empty it — in the folders _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash on the flash and in appdata. The pictures she hung stay too.

help.order_text: Templates first, then stacks, then appdata. A folder counts as in use as long as a template or stack names it — once those are gone, it shows up here.
help.trash_text: Nothing is deleted right away. What you put away is renamed into a folder _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash on the same disk — templates and stacks on the flash, appdata folders in the appdata share itself. That takes no time and no extra space, and "Put back" undoes it. Only "Empty" deletes for good.
help.templates_text: Leftover: no container and no image. Unused: no container, but the image is still there. Duplicate: an older file with the same <Name>. A template whose container exists is in use.
help.stacks_text: Matched with the containers by project name, the way the Compose Manager names them. Paths and images come from docker compose config, with the .env. A stack with containers is stopped (compose down) before it is put away; named volumes stay.
help.appdata_text: A folder is in use as soon as something names it: a container's mount, any template, a stack (with its .env), a compose file outside the Compose Manager, a VM, or any file on the flash (User Scripts, plugin settings …). A container that mounts the whole share doesn't count.
help.check_text: Nothing uses it, but: something has the same name, it is only mentioned in caches or the shell history, or something was written there in the last 30 days.
help.sizes_text: I count files and sizes in the background — folders to look at on my own, folders in use when you ask. Sleeping disks stay asleep; "Wake & look" wakes them when you want.
help.safe_text: While a backup runs I change nothing. I only ever rename — where that isn't possible (another disk, a dataset of its own) I refuse instead of copying.

help.icons_text: Containers that show a question mark on Unraid's Docker page and Dashboard: no picture set, or one Unraid can't load. For a container from a template I set the <Icon> in its template (shown at once); for one from a Compose Manager stack, the label in the stack's override file (lasting from its next Compose Up). Pictures come from this server (named like the app in Unraid's dockerMan/images folder; Apple's Time Machine logo for Time Machine containers), from Community Applications on this server, a table of well-known images (a database in an app's stack gets its database's logo) and, once checked, a guess from the image's name — addresses from the open dashboard-icons collection; nothing is bundled. Or upload your own in a container's details: your browser makes a square PNG of at most 256 × 256 pixels, I keep it on the flash in the office's folder and set it from there. Before I change a file, it goes into my storeroom.
help.loop_text: This version doesn't ship the question mark it shows for containers without a picture, and its pages ask for it endlessly — /var/log fills up within minutes. While that is so, I offer a stand-in (in RAM, gone after a reboot); once Unraid fixes it, my warning goes away.

errors.cleanup_icon_fallback_not_needed: No stand-in needed — Unraid has its question.png, or this version doesn't need one.
errors.cleanup_icon_fallback_failed: Could not put a stand-in at {path}.
section.leftovers_sub: What Mr. Restori left next to what he brought back — he never throws anything away either. Per restore, straight from his journals.

lo.where.one: From Mr. Restori's journal of 1 restore — I only look where he says he put something, never on a sleeping disk.
lo.where.other: From Mr. Restori's journals of {n} restores — I only look where he says he put something, never on a sleeping disk.

lo.undone_text: Mr. Restori has put this restore back already — what is left of it he no longer needs.
lo.what.aside_text: What was there before the restore — he renamed it aside (<name>.aside-<time>) instead of deleting it.
lo.what.putback_text: What was there when he put a restore back — renamed aside (<name>.putback-<time>).
lo.what.restored_text: The copy he restored next to the live one (<name>.restored-<time>) — you wanted to look at it; it stays until you say so.
lo.what.file_aside_text: A file he replaced, renamed aside next to it (<file>.restored-aside-<time>).
lo.what.flash_text: Templates and compose files he replaced on the flash, in /boot/config/_UnraidSecretaryOffice-restore/<time>/.
lo.what.libvirt_text: A VM's definition, NVRAM or TPM state he replaced, in /etc/libvirt/_UnraidSecretaryOffice-restore/<time>/.
lo.what.safety_text: The database dumps he made right before the restore, in the backup place (restore/<app>/<time>/).
lo.way_back_text: Mr. Restori's «Put back» of this restore still needs it. In my storeroom he can't find it — put it back from there first if you want to undo the restore.
lo.unknown_text: It lies where I can't look right now (a sleeping disk, or libvirt.img while the VM service is off).
cat.leftovers.way_back_text: «Put back» of its restore still needs it
cat.leftovers.unknown_text: On a sleeping disk, or the VM service is off
why.own_fs_text: Between it and its share lies a filesystem of its own — renaming can't reach my storeroom from there, so I leave it alone.
errors.cleanup_own_fs: {name} lies on a filesystem of its own — renaming can't move it into my storeroom.

park.text_leftovers.other: These {n} things go into my storeroom:

park.in_use_leftovers: Still Mr. Restori's way back: {names}. His «Put back» of those restores won't find them until you put them back from my storeroom.
park.where_leftovers: Each stays on its own pool or disk, in _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash of its share (what lies on the flash or in libvirt.img goes into my storeroom there); datasets are renamed next to it. Only renamed, nothing is copied — put back any time until you empty the storeroom.
empty.leftovers: Mr. Restori left nothing lying around. A tidy man!
help.leftovers_text: Mr. Restori never deletes anything either: what a restore replaces he renames aside (.aside-<time>, at «Put back» .putback-<time>), a copy lands next to the live one (.restored-<time>), files on the flash and in libvirt.img go into his folders _UnraidSecretaryOffice-restore, and of databases he makes safety dumps. Dust, all of it — but you never know: I only put it into my storeroom. I find it in his journals, never by searching the disks. What his «Put back» still needs is marked «his way back».
